title: Research: certify coupled factory scales and exact gauge floor
body:
## Summary

Delaying two doublings together in Alluri's retained PR681 eight-register factory circuit changes two nonunit additions into unit additions. Each move alone is cost-neutral; together they reduce the PR696 primitive cost from 81 to 77 per real-component block while retaining 34 scalar macros.

This contribution supplies the explicit circuit, an exact certificate for a broader restricted rescaling class, fresh reconstruction of all 14 raw-factory windows, complete primitive replay, negative controls, and local cost accounting.

No new κ. The selected conditional κ remains 0.001661634653669567.

## Exact result

Using Sagar Thakrar's PR696 lowering:

- Complete forward primitive count: 123,768 → 123,544.
- Complete backward/inverse-transpose count: 123,784 → 123,560.
- Saving: 224 per orientation, including inverse cleanups and both real components.
- Scalar macros remain 15,512; helpers 492; registers 716; centers 8; recursive children 3,472; adapter allowance 320,000.
- Exact prefix row-l1 maxima remain 124/107; fractional depth remains two bits.
- The retained conservative local PR696 recount falls from 8,298,987,643,784 to 8,298,987,643,560.

These are exact operation counts and a local recount, not runtime measurements or an executed global invoice.

A 57-vertex, 92-edge integer primal/dual certificate proves minimum absolute tension 9 for all integer dyadic wire gauges on the fixed ordered-addition topology, with identity boundary gauges, the two original negations, and per-addition work clearing retained. The resulting exact class minima are 123 original-Horner primitives and 67 PR696 primitives.

The 67-primitive witness uses 38 macros. Its additional adapter charges make the complete local PR696 bound 46,474,329,328 worse. It is retained as a valid but inferior accounting control. The useful 77-primitive witness preserves 34 macros; no optimality under that macro budget is claimed.

## Relationship to previous and concurrent work

PR681 provides the original circuit and raw-window/native checking machinery. PR696 provides the accepted lowering. Their integrated composition supplies the baseline.

The new evidence is the coupled neutral-move construction, the unbounded fixed-topology gauge certificate, the adverse complete-cost control, and complete PR696 primitive replay with arbitrary private inputs.

Concurrent PR922 by @CubeJerry, observed at efd5643c0016b6c6dac26e9ed7dee8a75295ff2a, reports a different 32-macro construction using three-register contractions and the same marginal PR696 saving of 224. Those topology changes lie outside this certificate's class. This submission claims neither superiority nor priority; compatibility and additive savings are untested. PR922 was not independently replayed here.

The overlap record also distinguishes prior single-scale, coefficient-work reuse, within-macro lowering, and X4 precondition work. Pending savings are not added to this result.

SOURCE-PINS.json pins all 16 consumed inputs. At final refresh, upstream/main was 91a2094f2e022930069e8cfdc810a3ea1b81cd09; all consumed inputs and the selected κ were unchanged.

OS-random assignment seed: 38, complex-supplier track. CLAIM.json records three candidate tasks, the local claim, and the evidence-driven macro-budget revision. No pinned sprint coordination issue was available.

## Reproduction

From the repository root:

    python3 -I -B research/complex-factory-gauge38/verify.py

Expected final line:

    PASS_COMPLEX_FACTORY_GAUGE38 baseline=81 budget=77 class_optimum=67 controls=46 blocks=14 saved=224,224 local_bill_delta=-224 no_new_kappa

Normal verification uses only the Python standard library and does not trust or require an optimization solver.

Optional nomination used NumPy 2.3.5 and SciPy 1.17.0: one LP followed by one 20-second-bounded macro-budget MILP. NOMINATION.json records the domain, stopping rule and completed coverage. Exact certificate verification establishes the result; the bounded search does not establish macro-budget optimality.

## Tests executed

PASS on Linux, CPython 3.12.14:

- Full verifier normally and under -O, matching the frozen receipt.
- All four local circuit orientations.
- Fresh raw construction, all 14 physical windows, and inherited scalar/frame/wrapper auditors.
- Six complete primitive projections: baseline, useful candidate and accounting control, both orientations; 725 arbitrary input columns each.
- 46 local rejection controls, including malformed duals, unpaid gauges, false prices, missing restoration, uncleared work, and deletion of each candidate gate.
- One corrupted physical-frame rejection.
- Four inherited negative controls per rebuilt native word.
- Two valid cost-neutral single-move controls.
- Nine package tests, including full optimized replay from a minimal checkout without Git metadata, paths containing spaces, repacked gzip inputs, corruption rejection and output preservation.
- Optional nomination, make selected-record-check, Python compilation and whitespace checks.

No implementation or mathematical check remains failed. The initially nominated 67-primitive circuit failed the useful-total-cost objective; that outcome is preserved explicitly.

## Scope and limitations

This package concerns the historical raw factory. Later selected-provider transport, Clifford phase lowering, whole-owner/global invoices and outer assembly were not rebuilt.

Uniform compilation, realization/hosting, recursive precision and tape accounting, exact recovery, and analytic transfer assumptions remain inherited. Finite replay is not formal verification of the multiplication theorem. The gauge bound is not unrestricted circuit optimality.

Not run: full make verify, selected frontier799 cold replay, global integration, Lean, another Python version or remote CI.

Only this research package is added. upstream/, selected records, generators and unrelated artifacts are unchanged.
